transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good morning. Let's talk about your presentation on volunteering. What approach are you planning?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We'd like to compare volunteering among young people and older people. We found a survey showing that people over sixty-five volunteer more hours than anyone else.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: But I'm worried that the survey is a few years old. The pandemic might have changed things.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good point, Jake. Is there a newer survey?

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: There's one from last year, but it only covers one region of the country.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Then you could mention both and explain the limits of each. That would show critical thinking. What else are you planning?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We'd like to interview some volunteers. I know a woman who works in a charity shop twice a week, and Jake knows a student who helps at a food bank.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Excellent. Interviews will make your presentation more interesting. How long will you spend on each part?

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We have fifteen minutes in total. We thought five minutes for the survey results, five for the interviews, and five for the conclusion.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I'd change that. The interviews are your own research, so they deserve more time. Perhaps six minutes for the survey, eight for the interviews, and only one minute for the conclusion.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: One minute is very short for a conclusion.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: True, but if your discussion is clear, the conclusion can be brief. Just give two or three key points.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: All right. Should we use slides?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, but keep them simple. No more than six words per line, and use pictures or charts rather than long text.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Handouts are optional. If you make one, keep it to a single page.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: Okay. When do we need to send you the draft?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: By the end of next week, please. And practise at least twice before the day. Ask a friend to time you.
